raw_response:
I've been farming this land for 40 years — since I was 22. My father handed me these 16 mu, and I've learned every patch of it. Some spots are a bit sandy and dry out faster, others hold water better. I know where the wheat grows tall and where I need to watch out.

My wife and I are the only ones at home now. Our son works in Shijiazhuang, sends some money back but not much. So it's the two of us, and I'm 62 now — my back isn't what it used to be. I can still do the planting and spraying, but for the heavy harvest work and hauling bags, I need to hire help. That costs money, so I have to watch every yuan.

I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension agent says when he comes by. But honestly? I trust my own eyes more than any brochure. Last year my wheat made about 420 kg per mu, and the maize did around 450 kg per mu. Not a great year, not a bad one. The wheat price was decent though, so we got by.

**Wheat:** I'll plant around October 12th, same as always. The neighbor Wang uses a new variety, but I'm sticking with what I know — the improved Jinmai variety that's reliable. Seed costs about 35 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer as base before planting — that's about 50 jin (25 kg) of 15-15-15 compound per mu, gives me some N, P, and K together. Then at jointing in March, I'll topdress with about 20 jin (10 kg) of urea per mu if the wheat looks green and healthy. If it looks yellow, maybe a bit more. Total N works out to about 16 kg per mu. I know the extension guy says I could do more, but fertilizer is expensive and I've got the maize season to think about too.

I'll irrigate three times for wheat: once before winter to help it establish, once at jointing, and once at grain filling if it doesn't rain. Each time costs me pumping fees — about 25 yuan per mu. Three times is enough; four would be better but I can't afford it. I'll spray herbicide once in spring, and maybe fungicide if I see rust showing up.

**Maize:** This is the tricky part. The wheat comes off around June 10th, and I need that maize in the ground by June 16th at the latest. Sometimes I don't even have time to plow properly — I just plant right after the combine goes through, maybe light rotary tillage if I can manage it. I buy hybrid seed, about 45 yuan per mu. It's more expensive than saving seed, but the yield is worth it.

For maize fertilizer, I'll put compound fertilizer in the row at planting — about 40 jin (20 kg) per mu. If I have time and the weather looks dry, I might side-dress some urea when the maize is knee-high, but honestly, sometimes I just do it all at planting because the window is so tight. That gives me about 14 kg N per mu. The maize usually gets two irrigations: one right after planting to help it germinate, and one at the big trumpet stage in August if it's dry. Some years one is enough if the rains come.

Pesticide for maize is just herbicide — I spray once when the maize is small. The weeds here aren't too bad if you catch them early.

**Labor:** My wife and I do most of the work. For wheat, we need about 18 family days between planting, managing, and helping with harvest. I hire a combine for harvest — that's 4 days of hired labor including hauling. For maize, the harvest is manual or semi-manual, so I hire 5 days of help. Family does about 12 days for maize. Hired labor is 120 yuan per day now, keeps going up.

**Money:** Total input costs this year will be around 8,200 yuan. That's seed, fertilizer, irrigation pumping, pesticide, and hired help. It's a lot for us. I thought about cutting back on fertilizer to save money, but last time I did that the wheat was thin and I lost more in yield than I saved. Better to borrow a bit from my brother if I have to than risk a bad crop.

The maize-wheat system is our insurance. If one fails, the other usually carries us through. I don't try anything fancy — no new crops, no big experiments. At my age, stability is everything.
